recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for a filtered registry link or registry UI change should be handled as a new issue or registry/product enhancement, not as unresolved work for FHIR-43508.
issue_request: FHIR-43508 was an Applied FHIR-core change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for clearer guidance on finding and reusing SubscriptionTopic definitions at registry.fhir.org because few canonical topics were available. The accepted resolution was to add a note that SubscriptionTopic definition is still in early adoption and that more topics will appear as IGs are published; comments also asked that implementer-authored topics not be excluded.
initial_application: Commit e159fa1d9dae5d4e15b5bb211d7ab7965a691494 added the requested note to source/subscriptions.html. Later commit fc659be95edf49f9c1bcc4dfb2f9a631ea45e06a reformatted and broadened the Subscriptions Framework page while preserving that registry/adoption guidance.
additional_context: source/subscriptions.html is in the current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml and the active Subscription, SubscriptionStatus, and SubscriptionTopic resources in source/fhir.ini. Current lines 390-400 still link to registry.fhir.org, recommend reuse and submission of topics, note early SubscriptionTopic adoption, explain growth through published IGs and registered topics, and encourage implementers to contribute topic definitions. FHIR-I Confluence minutes record the 14-0-0 Persuasive with Modification motion, and targeted Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The audit commit records that the current built source already satisfies the Jira resolution and the implementer-versus-IG-author nuance raised in comments.

related_jiras.note: This later subscription terminology/disambiguation change reworked and reformatted source/subscriptions.html after FHIR-43508 while preserving the registry/adoption note. It was background evidence only, not a separate decision here.
